finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::the "only our panel's checks" filter on the fix prompt is app-slug based, and every workflow in the repo — including one added on the untrusted branch — produces app slug `github-actions`
evidence: I read the supplied `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml` (the "Gather failing lens findings" step, and the identical `mine = (r) => NAMES.has(r.name) && r.app && r.app.slug === 'github-actions'` predicate in the round-bound guard). The claim's reading of the code is accurate: `github-actions` is the app slug for every GITHUB_TOKEN/workflow-created check run in the repository, so the filter proves only "some workflow in this repo made it", not "our trusted review-panel job made it", and the resulting `output.summary` is spliced verbatim into the fixer prompt for a Bash/Write-enabled agent — so the comment's assurance holds only against the narrower "another installed App" threat it names. The exploit path the reviewer describes is however gated in practice, as the reviewer itself concedes: adding/modifying a file under `.github/workflows` requires `workflows: write`, and the fix job's token is explicitly scoped to contents/pull-requests/issues, so today this is a latent defence-in-depth gap rather than a live injection channel (I could not check the installation's permission set — `docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md` was withheld). Note also that the flagged lines are pre-existing code, untouched by this diff, which only adds `allowed_bots` and the `fix` dependency for `stalled`.
